primary_claim: Simple probes could classify text 'genre' from mean latent activations of Mistral 7B Instruct with high F1 (up to 98% on CORE, 71% on synthetic data), but probes on a randomly-initialized model performed almost as well, and attempts to predict future paragraph-scale latent activations from early-token activations were largely unsuccessful.

effect.metric: F1 score (genre classification from mean activations)

limitations_stated: attention-pattern analysis (Experiment 2) was limited to a small number of texts (~2) and would benefit from a larger-scale study
genre probes appear to draw more on spurious correlations than on meaningful semantic features
heatmap-based evaluation may not be a reliable evaluation method, since lower training loss did not visibly correspond to better heatmaps
authors felt they erred toward running more experiments quickly rather than spending more time deciding what experiments to run
quote: We are able to extract text genre, but the probes seem to draw more on spurious correlations than on meaningful semantic features.
